rationale: The buyer is a real, named business role (DevOps engineer or cloud security lead at a company already paying for AWS and PrismaCloud) with genuine recurring pain — CSPM alert noise is a compliance and audit headache that happens continuously. Willingness to pay is solid: companies already spend on tooling in this space and Terraform modules / SaaS jit-access tools like Sym, ConductorOne, and Indent charge $5–20k/year, so the segment clearly pays. However, the core blocker is autonomy: delivering a working just-in-time IAM elevation solution requires reading customer AWS environments, generating or reviewing Terraform configs, and validating against their specific CSPM rule set — this is per-customer, technically bespoke work that Claude cannot fully automate without meaningful integration and security review, meaning operational_autonomy (4) and buildability_with_ai (4) both fall below their build_gate floors (7 and 6 respectively). The idea validates well but cannot be built as a hands-off micro-service in its current framing.
solution_plan: The micro-service would be a 'JIT IAM Advisor': a customer inputs their PrismaCloud alert JSON and their current IAM group/policy setup via a web form, and Claude produces a tailored, copy-paste-ready Terraform module or AWS CDK snippet implementing a break-glass/just-in-time access pattern that resolves the specific alert. BUILD: The factory builds a landing page with a file-upload/textarea intake form, a Claude prompt chain that parses the alert + IAM context and outputs the remediation template with explanations, and a Stripe payment link (one-time $49–149 per remediation report). SELL: Target DevOps leads and cloud security engineers via Hacker News 'Ask HN', Reddit r/devops and r/aws, and direct outreach to companies posting CSPM-related questions on ServerFault/Stack Overflow; all outreach batches require Youval's approval before sending. MAINTAIN: Delivery is automated — the form triggers Claude, the report is emailed back; billing is Stripe self-serve; Claude handles FAQ support replies. The recurring human touch is approving outreach batches and reviewing any reports flagged as low-confidence by Claude. CAVEAT: The core problem here is that 'one-size' Terraform templates rarely fully satisfy a specific customer's CSPM configuration without iteration — if repeat revisions are needed per customer, operational autonomy breaks down and this becomes consulting. Validate first by selling 3–5 one-shot reports and measuring how much back-and-forth each requires before deciding whether to productize further.
notes: Two build_gates fail: operational_autonomy=4 (below floor of 7) and buildability_with_ai=4 (below floor of 6). The solution inherently requires per-customer AWS environment context and iterative validation against the customer's specific CSPM ruleset, making fully automated, hands-off delivery difficult. Stage capped at 'validate'. Validate by selling a few one-shot paid reports to measure revision load before investing in a full product build.
